answer_q: How can professional services firms use AI?
answer: Professional services firms use AI to draft proposals and tender responses, summarise meetings into actions, keep CRM records current, search past projects and templates, prepare client reports and automate onboarding and admin. Senior staff review client-facing work and keep responsibility for advice.
body:
Billable time is your scarcest resource

In a professional services firm, every hour senior people spend on admin is an hour not spent with clients. Proposals are rebuilt from scratch, meeting actions get lost, CRM records go stale and the firm’s best past work is buried in folders nobody can search.

AI handles the drafting, summarising and searching, so your experts can focus on judgement, relationships and delivery.

Where AI helps professional services firms most

Proposals and tenders

AI reads the brief or tender, extracts requirements and drafts responses from your past bids, case studies and team profiles for expert review. See custom AI agents.

Meeting follow-up

Meeting notes or recordings become summaries, action lists and CRM updates, sent to the right people automatically. See CRM automation.

Knowledge search

Staff ask questions across past projects, methods and templates and get answers with links to the source documents. See LLM, RAG & knowledge-base bots.

Client reporting

Recurring client reports are assembled from your systems with an AI-written summary for review. See AI workflow automation.

Onboarding and admin

New client and new project set-up, engagement letters and timesheet reminders run automatically. See business process automation.

Human-backed AI employees for professional services firms

Most professional services firms don’t want another tool to supervise. Our AI Employees service builds the AI around your firm, then runs it with a dedicated Crenosoft team that learns your services, clients and rules. The AI handles routine work; our reviewers handle anything unusual, around the clock; and decisions that belong to you come to your nominated person with a clear summary. We agree an hours-saved target up front and report against it every month.

Software we connect to

We connect with CRMs such as HubSpot and Salesforce, practice and project tools such as WorkflowMax-style platforms, Asana and Monday.com, Microsoft 365, SharePoint, Teams, Google Workspace and meeting tools that produce transcripts.

Client confidentiality and quality control

Client documents stay inside controlled systems, with access limited by client and project. AI-drafted proposals and reports are always reviewed by the responsible professional before they leave the firm, and providers are configured to keep data out of model training where available. Governance follows the Australian Government’s Guidance for AI Adoption.

Across every project we follow the Privacy Act 1988, the OAIC’s guidance on commercially available AI products and our own Responsible AI Policy.

Building on your firm’s knowledge

Your firm’s past proposals, reports and project files are a valuable asset that is usually hard to use. A knowledge-base assistant turns that material into something staff can ask questions of, with links to the original documents. New team members get up to speed faster, proposals reuse the best of past work, and senior people stop being interrupted for information that is already written down somewhere.

Results we measure for firms

Before we build, we record a baseline of how long the work takes and how often it happens. After launch, your monthly report tracks the numbers that matter to firms:

  • Proposal preparation time per submission
  • Meeting actions captured and completed
  • CRM record completeness
  • Knowledge searches answered with sources
  • Senior hours returned to client work

These figures sit alongside hours saved and accuracy, so you can see exactly what the AI is contributing and where our team is still stepping in.

Recruitment, engineering, architecture and consulting firms each have their own workflows, but the pattern is the same: experts spend too long preparing documents and updating systems. We start with the task that costs your senior people the most hours each month, prove the time saving, and then extend AI across the firm one workflow at a time.

Firm leaders also get clearer visibility of pipeline, proposal win rates and where senior time is really going each month.

How to get started

  1. Free AI audit: 30 minutes to map your busiest workflows and pick the first opportunity.
  2. Blueprint and fixed quote: what the AI will do, which systems it connects to and the price in AUD.
  3. Build and test: usually two to six weeks, tested on real examples from your firm.
  4. Launch and improve: monthly reports on hours saved, accuracy and improvements.

Not sure where to begin? Start with an AI Readiness Assessment, or see how we work locally on our Melbourne AI agency page.
faqs: Can AI write proposals and tender responses?
AI can extract requirements and draft responses from your past bids and case studies, cutting preparation time. Your experts review and finalise every submission.
Can AI keep our CRM up to date?
Yes. Meeting summaries, emails and actions can update CRM records automatically, so pipeline reports stay accurate without manual entry.
We keep client documents in controlled systems with access limited by client and project, and configure AI providers to keep data out of model training where available.
What is the best first AI project for a firm?
Meeting follow-up and knowledge search are popular first projects, because they save senior time every week with low risk.
